label: Early-mid original-phase steps (t=3-5) on inputs e/w/u/t/a/k/c/v/n
explanation: Fires almost only during the original input phase (99.5% of mass), never at t=0-1 and never in the copy phase, with a small tail at the <DEL> step. It peaks at original positions 3-5 (about 80% of mass across t=2-6) and falls away after t=7. Within that window it is driven by the input token: e and w are strongest (rate about 25%, together 40% of mass), then u and t, then a, k, c, v, n. It favours first occurrences of a token (89% of mass). Sequences that start with 3 or l have higher rates (about 2.8x), and the largest activations (e or w at t=3-4 after a 3/l start) come from those. Rates fall with more digits. The predicate is a coarse window-times-token-set description that plateaus near F1 0.56 on dev. The unit looks like a graded function of position, current token and sequence prefix, so precision and recall both stay incomplete.
